_README: Structure and metadata for Mao Dun's Midnight (子夜). The build is driven ENTIRELY by this file. Chapter ids start with 'ch'. A chapter is treated as translated once out/<id>_reading.md exists. The 19 numbered chapters map 1:1 to the source spine files Text/part0002.xhtml .. part0020.xhtml; the afterword (后记) is part0021.xhtml.
description: An annotated English translation of Mao Dun's 子夜 (Midnight), the landmark 1933 novel of Shanghai in 1930: a panoramic realist portrait of the industrialist Wu Sunfu, the speculators of the bond market, the silk filatures and their strikes, and a Chinese bourgeoisie caught between foreign capital and revolution. This edition carries footnotes, a glossary, and an honest apparatus for uncertain and editorial passages.
subjects: Chinese literature — 20th century — Translations into English
_source_note: Source is a digital EPUB (no OCR): 子夜 by 茅盾. Spine (24 docs): cover_page + 版权信息 (part0000, colophon) + 目录 (part0001, the source's own table of contents) + the 19 chapters (part0002..part0020) + 后记 (part0021, afterword) + part0022, which collects the SOURCE'S OWN 9 endnotes, keyed by bracketed markers [1]..[9] that appear inline in the chapters (e.g. [1] at 'Light, Heat, Power!' in Chapter One). Those are the author's/editor's notes: during translation they must be rendered as the SOURCE's own notes (distinct from the translator's footnotes), placed at their markers. The cover, 版权信息 and 目录 are not translatable units and are not in 'structure'; the builder generates its own title page and TOC.
source_edition: 子夜, first published January 1933 by 开明书店 (Kaiming Bookstore), Shanghai; title calligraphy by Ye Shengtao. Written October 1931 – December 1932 (per the afterword). Digital EPUB edition.
_translator_note: Rendered verbatim as the Translator's Note page. Inline .. honored; use NUMERIC character references, never named entities.
translator_note: This is an English translation of 子夜 (Midnight), Mao Dun's 1930-Shanghai novel, made from the digital source edition. The book was written between October 1931 and December 1932 and first published by the Kaiming Bookstore in January 1933.

The source carries nine of its own notes, gathered at the end of the original and keyed to bracketed markers in the text; these glosses of foreign words and period slang are the author's, and are kept visibly distinct from the translator's footnotes. Names follow pinyin except where a conventional English form exists, with one rendering per referent fixed in the glossary. Where a passage is genuinely ambiguous, the choice is stated in a note and nothing is invented to smooth it over.
